summary: This Nexus Innovations Inc. policy document sets remote work communication and collaboration standards. It covers daily check-ins and response times, virtual meeting etiquette, collaboration tool usage, communication tone, and cross-departmental projects. Non-compliance may lead to a review of the remote work arrangement and disciplinary action.
one_line: Nexus Innovations Inc. policy defining remote work communication, meeting, tool, tone, and cross-department collaboration standards, with consequences for non-compliance.
key_facts: Nexus Innovations Inc. requires all team members to check in via the designated communication platform each morning.
Employees must be available during core business hours defined by their team's time zone.
Employees must respond to emails, messages, and calls within one business hour, unless in pre-scheduled meetings or deep work sessions.
Employees must use out-of-office notifications or update their status when unavailable.
Virtual meeting rules at Nexus include being punctual, using video when possible, and muting microphones when not speaking.
Meeting organizers must prepare and circulate an agenda in advance, take minutes, and send a recap with action items to all participants.
Employees must be proficient with the chosen communication and project management platforms and keep tasks and projects regularly updated.
Work-in-progress documents should be shared in shared spaces to encourage real-time feedback, while respecting data privacy and confidentiality.
Communication style should be clear, concise, respectful, and constructive, and employees should seek clarification rather than make assumptions.
Cross-departmental projects require a project lead as main point of contact, regular check-ins, clearly defined roles, and shared calendars for milestones and deadlines.
Remote communication must comply with broader remote work policies on data security, confidentiality, and work hours.
Non-compliance may result in a review of the employee's remote work arrangement and potential disciplinary action.
Questions should go to the employee's direct supervisor or the Human Resources department.
